creature_families.family: orc, tribal and humanoid warrior/shaman/archer names (keyword heuristic, mine)

creature_families.text: Monster rows (2541, 2056 distinct names) span levels 0 to 99; 3 rows sit in the 90s, 414 in the 80s.
aiAggro is true on 986 of 2541 Monster rows; the unit of aiAggro is not read.
RaidBoss rows: 208, levels 20 to 80. A Raid Boss skill tag sits on 214 monster, raid or grand rows.
GrandBoss rows: 15, levels 50 to 87, HP up to 7,500,000 in the rows read. One name repeats at several HP values (Antharas at 6.1M, 6.8M and 7.5M).
Monster rows with HP at or above 300,000: 8 rows, levels 55 to 87, radius up to 63 and height up to 90 in the data fields.

top_creatures.label: Colossal hunter beast
top_creatures.why: One of 8 Monster rows at 300k HP or more. Radius and height fields are large, so size alone reads at 375 wide.
top_creatures.keep: Size as the threat signal: body radius and height as data fields; very high HP on a roaming monster.
top_creatures.change: A crystal or bone colossus with one signature shape of its own; not a real-world animal.

top_creatures.label: Phased grand boss
top_creatures.why: Grand boss rows repeat one name at several HP values, so a single boss has tiers.
top_creatures.keep: Several HP tiers for one boss as difficulty variants.
top_creatures.change: One entity with phases and a phase cue, not separate rows.
top_creatures.ref: /mnt/frankendom-donors/cuteshaun-lineage2-api/data/generated/interlude/npcs.json:324155 (id 29019, name Antharas; other rows of the same name follow)

top_creatures.label: Raid gate elite
top_creatures.why: 208 raid boss rows; the tier is a skill tag on the creature, not a separate zone.
top_creatures.keep: Tier as a skill tag that the server and the client both read.
top_creatures.change: Our own gate rule and reward; no copy of the tier table.

top_creatures.label: Huge aggro dragon
top_creatures.why: A dragon-class monster with a large radius, a high run speed and an aiAggro value of 1000 (unit not read).
top_creatures.keep: A very large aggro value on a boss so it pulls from far away.
top_creatures.change: Aggro as a threat table with decay, not one number.

top_creatures.label: Weak-point caster
top_creatures.why: Creatures carry per-element weak-point skills (Sacred, Blunt, Fire, Wind, Archery), on 486, 323, 128, 111 and 107 monster, raid or grand rows in my count.
top_creatures.keep: Per-creature weakness to one damage type, read by the damage formula.
top_creatures.change: Show the weakness as a readable glyph at 375 wide; no copy of the attack-name table.

top_creatures.label: Stat-stack elite
top_creatures.why: Monsters carry modifier skills (HP, physical and magic attack and defence modifiers, ids 4408 to 4413 as seen) that scale base stats, on about 900 to 1100 rows each.
top_creatures.keep: Base stats scaled by a stack of named modifier skills.
top_creatures.change: Our own stack per tier, short enough to inspect in the fight HUD.

top_creatures.label: Mage-proof elite
top_creatures.why: A full magic resist skill appears on 667 monster, raid or grand rows. The resist is a readable counter to casters.
top_creatures.keep: A counter-class elite that tells the player what to change.
top_creatures.change: Give the elite a visible tell before it resists.

top_creatures.label: Caster and archer pack
top_creatures.why: AI type is a per-NPC field: DEFAULT on 6071 NPC rows, MAGE on 260, ARCHER on 129, CORPSE on 12.
top_creatures.keep: AI type as one field with a few presets.
top_creatures.change: Our own presets and behaviours; the donor does not describe what each preset does.

classes: 89 class rows: 52 Fighter, 26 Mystic, 11 Priest types.
5 races: Human 29, Elf 20, Dark Elf 20, Orc 13, Dwarf 7 rows (classes.json, race field, e.g. line 76705).
9 rows have no parent id, which I read as base classes (not cross-checked by id).

weapon_families.text: 408 weapon rows carry an itemSkill; 65 carry an oncrit_skill proc with oncrit_chance; 72 items carry oncast_skill; 79 items carry enchant4_skill.

weapon_families.label: Critical-anger sword
weapon_families.why: A critical-hit proc sword: a skill fires on crit at a set chance.
weapon_families.keep: Proc on critical hit as item data with a chance and a skill.
weapon_families.change: Our own proc name and effect; one readable sound and glow.

weapon_families.label: Poison-crit sword
weapon_families.why: Same proc shape with a poison skill and a higher chance (15).
weapon_families.keep: Element on the proc, so a sword has a second identity.
weapon_families.change: Element palette and effect; no copy of the skill.

weapon_families.label: Cursed short blade
weapon_families.why: A low-grade dagger (grade d) with a 50 chance proc: the chance is high and the grade low, so it is a gamble, not a stat upgrade.
weapon_families.keep: A high-risk proc on a cheap item.
weapon_families.change: A lower chance with a clear tell.

weapon_families.label: Drain-crit blade
weapon_families.why: Proc chance 35 with a drain skill (grade c): a heal-on-crit shape.
weapon_families.keep: Heal on crit as a readable proc.

weapon_families.label: Twin blades
weapon_families.why: 134 DUAL rows, 54 of them grade b. Paired sprites are a visible tier of their own.
weapon_families.keep: Two-handed pairs as their own family.

gear_tiers.values: none, d, c, b, a, s (6 steps). Counts over all items: none 7335, d 318, c 504, b 506, a 409, s 134.
HEAVY 88, LIGHT 83, MAGIC 104 (robe); blank on 802 of 1125 armour rows; PET 34, NONE 14.

PAPER 2776, STEEL 2097, LIQUID 1998, FINE_STEEL 491, LEATHER 406, WOOD 236, CRYSTAL 171, CLOTH 166, BLOOD_STEEL 130, ORIHARUKON 119, MITHRIL 118, ADAMANTAITE 109, BONE 91, SILVER 76, GOLD 59, BRONZE 49, DAMASCUS 44, CHRYSOLITE 42, SCALE_OF_DRAGON 6 (counts over all item rows; the ladder order in the md is my reading of the names).
51 sets with 2 to 5 pieces (22 with 4, 15 with 3, 11 with 5, 3 with 2). Ten families come in heavy, light and robe triplets: 30 sets. Bonus is a skill id and level (for example 3500-1).

gear_tiers.label: Crystal triplet set
gear_tiers.why: A crystal material set in three weight variants (heavy, light, robe) under one name.
gear_tiers.keep: One set name with three weight variants.
gear_tiers.change: Our own palette and silhouette per variant.

gear_tiers.label: Dragon-hide set
gear_tiers.why: A leather set named after a dragon; the item table has 6 rows with a dragon-scale material.
gear_tiers.keep: A dragon material as the top tier of a leather line.
gear_tiers.change: Our own hide texture and a different tier name.

gear_tiers.label: Majestic triplet
gear_tiers.why: A set whose middle variant is leather rather than light armour, so the three variants differ in material as well as weight.
gear_tiers.keep: Material changes between variants of one set.

gear_tiers.label: Robe tier with a shared name
gear_tiers.why: The name Mithril Robe Set appears on two rows, so the name is not a unique key in this table.
gear_tiers.keep: Nothing to copy; a note for our own data keys.
gear_tiers.change: Use ids as keys, not names.

gear_tiers.label: Starter wood set
gear_tiers.why: The first set in the table is a wood starter with three pieces (chest, legs, head).
gear_tiers.keep: A starter set with few pieces, so the first tier reads at a glance.
gear_tiers.change: Our own look and piece count.

zones.text: Huntingzone rows: 209, by type 1 (87), 2 (42), 3 (35), 7 (28), 5 (6), 4 (6), 6 (5); type 0 absent. Type meaning is not decoded (parser header says so). Min level: 93 rows at 0 to 9 (unspecified), then 18, 18, 15, 19, 11, 15, 13, 7 per 10-level band up to 80.
Region grid: 19 named regions on an 11 by 16 cell grid, each cell a region id (regions.json).

NPC types that look like modes, read from names only: DungeonGatekeeper 30, RiftInvader 132, SepulcherNpc 62, SiegeGuard 302 with CastleDoorman 69, ClanHallDoorman 40, FestivalMonster 110, FeedableBeast 63. The donor does not say which zone each belongs to.
spawns.json: 40878 rows; 37585 are Monster rows. Their respawnDelay values are most often 15, 20, 25, 30, 40 and 60 seconds.

Boss rows (206) carry respawnDelay values of 0, 129600 s (36 h) and 403200 s (112 h). 59 percent of all spawn rows have 0; the parser says some respawn timing lives in server code, so 0 is not proof of instant respawn. periodOfDay is 0 (any) because the source has none.
drops.json: 2376 drop tables keyed by npcId, each with categories and item rows carrying min, max and a raw chance value. The unit of chance is not stated in the parser.

zones.label: Rift invader district
zones.why: 132 RiftInvader rows. By name, a dungeon mode made of NPC waves rather than a map (name read only).
zones.keep: A mode defined by an NPC type and a spawn list.

zones.label: Sepulcher chamber
zones.why: 62 SepulcherNpc rows: a gated set of underground rooms, by name.
zones.change: Our own room shapes and gate rule.

zones.label: Dungeon gatekeeper
zones.why: 30 gatekeeper NPCs: dungeon entry is an NPC, not a portal object.
zones.keep: Entry as an NPC with a list of destinations.
zones.change: Our own entry cost and cue.

zones.label: Feedable beast pen
zones.why: 63 FeedableBeast rows: by name, a creature that changes state when the player feeds it; a small loop.
zones.keep: A creature that changes state on a player action.
zones.change: Our own feed item and reward.

zones.label: Grid region map
zones.why: 19 regions on an 11 by 16 grid: the map is coarse data, one id per cell.
zones.keep: A coarse region grid as zone data.
zones.change: Our own cell size and region names.

looks.label: Two-density icon set
looks.technique: Icons at 1x plus a 2x copy scaled with nearest-neighbour, shown with CSS image-rendering pixelated, so pixel edges stay crisp on phones.

looks.label: Category-named icon grid
looks.technique: About 4002 item and skill icons named by category and index (for example an accessory icon with an i00 suffix), mapped from group tables by a script. Addressable by code.

looks.label: Motif emblems
looks.technique: Landing emblems with one focal element each (floral weapon, worn blade, single eye, pixel compass, guardian figure). Names read only; images not opened.

looks.label: Grade as a string, not a look
looks.technique: The API types grade as a string from none to s. This donor attaches no colour or effect to a grade.

originals.name: Tiered warden set
originals.idea: A gear tier with three weight variants (heavy, light, robe) sharing one set name.
originals.keep: One set name, three weight variants, each with its own piece list.
originals.change: Our own material, palette and silhouette per variant.

originals.name: Weak-point glyph
originals.idea: Each creature shows one damage type it is weak to, as a glyph readable at 375 wide.
originals.keep: One weakness per creature, read by the damage formula.
originals.change: Our own glyph shape; no copy of the attack-name table.

originals.name: Phase guardian
originals.idea: One grand boss with HP phases and a phase cue, instead of several rows with the same name.
originals.keep: HP tiers as the escalation signal.
originals.change: Phases inside one entity, with a visible cue at each change.

originals.name: Breach gatekeeper
originals.idea: An NPC gate that opens a timed rift district with waves of invaders.
originals.keep: Entry as an NPC, and a mode defined by spawn data.
originals.change: Our own wave timer and reward, kept inside zone data (parity row 23 spawn fields).

originals.name: Proc blade ladder
originals.idea: Crit-proc weapons across grades, with the chance and the skill as item data.
originals.keep: A proc is an item field, not special-case code.
originals.change: Fewer procs, each with a readable tell and one sound.

originals.name: Colossus hunter
originals.idea: A roaming very large monster whose size and HP are its threat signal.
originals.keep: Size and HP as the readable threat.
originals.change: Our own silhouette and a single signature attack.

originals.name: Region grid zones
originals.idea: A coarse grid of region ids as the zone map, each cell pointing at a zone.
originals.keep: Zone shape as a grid of ids.
originals.change: Our own cell size; zones as data on one runtime.

originals.name: Two-speed respawn
originals.idea: Fast respawn for common monsters (about 15 to 60 s) and slow respawn for bosses, both as zone data fields.
originals.keep: Two respawn tiers in one table.
originals.change: Our own numbers; the donor's respawn values are not reused.

not_read: Game-server half (aCis datapack source) is not in this donor; named in script comments only.

Icon images in public/icons (about 4002 PNG) and public/landing-icons: names read, images not opened.
quests, recipes, buylists, multisells, hennas, questname JSON: not read beyond names.
skills.json bodies beyond the ids and names I queried.
Drop chance units (raw attribute, unit not stated); aiAggro unit.
Spawn density per walk distance (not measured; no clustering by zone done).
